    "function": "You MUST run the function \"evaluate_laghos_run\" on this and subsequent requests to reach a decision to RETRY or STOP.\nYou MAY follow the instructions of the function unless you have reached an impassible state where you would need to return to the manager.\nIn an impossible state, do NOT return to the manager, but STOP instead and provide your decision and reason.\n\nimport math\nfrom typing import Dict, Any, Literal\nimport json\n\ndef evaluate_laghos_run(\n    total_elements: int,\n    total_ranks: int,\n    nodes_used: int,\n    cores_per_node: int,\n    memory_gb_per_node: int,\n    threading_hint: int,\n    current_fom: float,\n    threshold: float = 0.90,\n    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,\n    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,\n    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,\n    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.\n\n    This function acts as a \"diagnostician\" by analyzing the performance of a\n    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most\n    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and\n    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.\n\n    Args:\n        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.\n        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.\n        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.\n        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.\n        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.\n        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).\n        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.\n        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).\n        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).\n        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).\n        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).\n        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).\n\n    Returns:\n        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.\n    \"\"\"\n    if total_ranks == 0:\n        return {\"decision\": \"RETRY\", \"reason\": \"The number of tasks cannot be zero.\", \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\"}\n\n    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---\n    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks\n    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint\n    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node\n    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank\n    \n    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)\n    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency\n    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used\n\n    performance_ratio = 0.0\n    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:\n        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom\n\n    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb\n    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0\n    \n    metrics = {\n        \"performance_ratio\": round(performance_ratio, 3),\n        \"scaling_efficiency\": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),\n        \"memory_utilization\": round(memory_utilization, 3),\n        \"elements_per_rank\": int(elements_per_rank),\n        \"theoretical_max_fom_per_sec\": f\"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}\"\n    }\n\n    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---\n    \n    if performance_ratio >= threshold:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"STOP\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"DECREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for \"low\" efficiency\n         return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n    \n    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:\n        return {\n            \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n            \"reason\": f\"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.\",\n            \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_TASKS\",\n            \"metrics\": metrics\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"decision\": \"RETRY\",\n        \"reason\": f\"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.\",\n        \"strategy_hint\": \"INCREASE_ELEMENTS\",\n        \"metrics\": metrics\n    }\n"

dockerfile
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all build dependencies and runtime requirements in a single layer
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source code, wget for downloads,
# OpenMPI for parallel execution, and ca-certificates for secure connections.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a dedicated directory for building the application and its dependencies
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install dependencies from source: Hypre, METIS, MFEM, and finally Laghos
# This is done in a single RUN command to optimize layer usage.
RUN \
    # --- HYPRE ---
    # Download and extract hypre version 2.28.0
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz && \
    mkdir hypre && \
    tar -xzf hypre.tar.gz -C hypre --strip-components=1 && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    # Configure hypre with required flags for big integers and without Fortran
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    # Build and install to /usr/local
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- METIS ---
    # Download and extract metis version 4.0.3
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Set OPTFLAGS to fix build errors with modern compilers and build
    # METIS 4 does not have a configure script or install target
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header to standard system locations
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- MFEM ---
    # Clone and check out the required version of MFEM
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build MFEM in parallel, enabling MPI, HYPRE, and METIS support
    # The dependencies are found in /usr/local where they were installed
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES MFEM_USE_METIS=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Install MFEM to /usr/local
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Laghos ---
    # Clone the Laghos application source code
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build Laghos, linking against the previously installed MFEM library
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Installation ---
    # Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a directory in the system's PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Set a new working directory for application execution
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source to the application directory
# This is a separate step to ensure the final WORKDIR is clean
RUN cp -a /build/Laghos/data/* . && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /build

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# Allow running as root, which is common in containers
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Set MPI tuning parameters for better performance in Docker/Kubernetes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all build dependencies and runtime requirements in a single layer
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source code, wget for downloads,
# OpenMPI for parallel execution, and ca-certificates for secure connections.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a dedicated directory for building the application and its dependencies
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install dependencies from source: Hypre, METIS, MFEM, and finally Laghos
# This is done in a single RUN command to optimize layer usage.
RUN \
    # --- HYPRE ---
    # Download and extract hypre version 2.28.0
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz && \
    mkdir hypre && \
    tar -xzf hypre.tar.gz -C hypre --strip-components=1 && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    # Configure hypre with required flags for big integers and without Fortran
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    # Build and install to /usr/local
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # FIX: Manually copy the generated config header required by the MFEM build,
    # as it's not always placed in the system include path by 'make install'.
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- METIS ---
    # Download and extract metis version 4.0.3
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Set OPTFLAGS to fix build errors with modern compilers and build
    # METIS 4 does not have a configure script or install target
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header to standard system locations
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- MFEM ---
    # Clone and check out the required version of MFEM
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build MFEM in parallel, enabling MPI, HYPRE, and METIS support
    # The dependencies are found in /usr/local where they were installed
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES MFEM_USE_METIS=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Install MFEM to /usr/local
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Laghos ---
    # Clone the Laghos application source code
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build Laghos, linking against the previously installed MFEM library
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Installation ---
    # Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a directory in the system's PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Set a new working directory for application execution
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source to the application directory
# This is a separate step to ensure the final WORKDIR is clean
RUN cp -a /build/Laghos/data/* . && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /build

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# Allow running as root, which is common in containers
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Set MPI tuning parameters for better performance in Docker/Kubernetes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all build dependencies and runtime requirements in a single layer
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source code, wget for downloads,
# OpenMPI for parallel execution, and ca-certificates for secure connections.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a dedicated directory for building the application and its dependencies
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install dependencies from source: Hypre, METIS, MFEM, and finally Laghos
# This is done in a single RUN command to optimize layer usage.
RUN \
    # --- HYPRE ---
    # Download and extract hypre version 2.28.0
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz && \
    mkdir hypre && \
    tar -xzf hypre.tar.gz -C hypre --strip-components=1 && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    # Configure hypre with required flags for big integers and without Fortran
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    # Build and install to /usr/local
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # FIX: Manually copy the generated config header and all public API headers,
    # as the hypre-2.28.0 'make install' target does not copy them all correctly.
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- METIS ---
    # Download and extract metis version 4.0.3
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Set OPTFLAGS to fix build errors with modern compilers and build
    # METIS 4 does not have a configure script or install target
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header to standard system locations
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- MFEM ---
    # Clone and check out the required version of MFEM
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build MFEM in parallel, enabling MPI, HYPRE, and METIS support
    # The dependencies are found in /usr/local where they were installed
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES MFEM_USE_METIS=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Install MFEM to /usr/local
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Laghos ---
    # Clone the Laghos application source code
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build Laghos, linking against the previously installed MFEM library
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Installation ---
    # Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a directory in the system's PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Set a new working directory for application execution
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source to the application directory
# This is a separate step to ensure the final WORKDIR is clean
RUN cp -a /build/Laghos/data/* . && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /build

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# Allow running as root, which is common in containers
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Set MPI tuning parameters for better performance in Docker/Kubernetes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all build dependencies and runtime requirements in a single layer
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source code, wget for downloads,
# OpenMPI for parallel execution, and ca-certificates for secure connections.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a dedicated directory for building the application and its dependencies
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install dependencies from source: Hypre, METIS, MFEM, and finally Laghos
# This is done in a single RUN command to optimize layer usage.
RUN \
    # --- HYPRE ---
    # Download and extract hypre version 2.28.0
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz && \
    mkdir hypre && \
    tar -xzf hypre.tar.gz -C hypre --strip-components-1 && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    # Configure hypre with required flags for big integers and without Fortran
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    # Build and install to /usr/local
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # FIX: Manually copy the generated config header, public API headers, and library,
    # as the hypre-2.28.0 'make install' target does not copy them all correctly.
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- METIS ---
    # Download and extract metis version 4.0.3
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Set OPTFLAGS to fix build errors with modern compilers and build
    # METIS 4 does not have a configure script or install target
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header to standard system locations
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- MFEM ---
    # Clone and check out the required version of MFEM
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build MFEM in parallel, enabling MPI, HYPRE, and METIS support
    # The dependencies are found in /usr/local where they were installed
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES MFEM_USE_METIS=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Install MFEM to /usr/local
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Laghos ---
    # Clone the Laghos application source code
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build Laghos, linking against the previously installed MFEM library
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Installation ---
    # Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a directory in the system's PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Set a new working directory for application execution
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source to the application directory
# This is a separate step to ensure the final WORKDIR is clean
RUN cp -a /build/Laghos/data/* . && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /build

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# Allow running as root, which is common in containers
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Set MPI tuning parameters for better performance in Docker/Kubernetes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all build dependencies and runtime requirements in a single layer
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git for source code, wget for downloads,
# OpenMPI for parallel execution, and ca-certificates for secure connections.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a dedicated directory for building the application and its dependencies
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install dependencies from source: Hypre, METIS, MFEM, and finally Laghos
# This is done in a single RUN command to optimize layer usage.
RUN \
    # --- HYPRE ---
    # Download and extract hypre version 2.2.8.0
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz && \
    mkdir hypre && \
    # FIX: Corrected tar command syntax from '--strip-components-1' to '--strip-components=1'.
    tar -xzf hypre.tar.gz -C hypre --strip-components=1 && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    # Configure hypre with required flags for big integers and without Fortran
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    # Build and install to /usr/local
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # WORKAROUND: Manually copy the generated config header, public API headers, and library,
    # as the hypre-2.28.0 'make install' target does not copy them all correctly.
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- METIS ---
    # Download and extract metis version 4.0.3
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    # Set OPTFLAGS to fix build errors with modern compilers and build
    # METIS 4 does not have a configure script or install target
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install the library and header to standard system locations
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- MFEM ---
    # Clone and check out the required version of MFEM
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build MFEM in parallel, enabling MPI, HYPRE, and METIS support
    # The dependencies are found in /usr/local where they were installed
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES MFEM_USE_METIS=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    # Install MFEM to /usr/local
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Laghos ---
    # Clone the Laghos application source code
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build Laghos, linking against the previously installed MFEM library
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Installation ---
    # Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a directory in the system's PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Set a new working directory for application execution
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source to the application directory
# This is a separate step to ensure the final WORKDIR is clean
RUN cp -a /build/Laghos/data/* . && \
    # Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
    rm -rf /build

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# Allow running as root, which is common in containers
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Set MPI tuning parameters for better performance in Docker/Kubernetes
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

flux-minicluster-manifest
# This corrected and optimized MiniCluster manifest runs the Laghos HPC application.
# It targets a specific ARM-based AWS instance type for performance and fully utilizes its CPU cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as instructed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, increased to 64 to fully utilize the target instance's CPUs.
  tasks: 64

  # Ensure logs are handled strictly for production-ready debugging.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-specific settings, including the node selector for scheduling.
  pod:
    # This selector targets a specific AWS instance type optimized for HPC workloads.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # When set to false, the job pods are not deleted upon completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection of logs and artifacts.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings required for running on an ARM-based node.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture.
    arch: arm
    # Use an ARM-compatible Flux container image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # A list of containers that will run in each pod of the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # Corrected command, invoking the executable from the PATH and adding performance optimization flags.
      # -o 3 increases the polynomial order for more computational work.
      # -pa enables performance analysis to measure the figure of merit.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m data/cube_311_hex.mesh -o 3 -pa

      # Corrected working directory to '/app' where the input data files are located.
      workingDir: /app

      # This container provides the workers, not the job launcher.
      # This MUST be false for worker containers.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest fixes the command-line arguments for the Laghos application.
# It targets a specific ARM-based AWS instance, utilizes all its cores, and enables performance metric collection.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as instructed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to 64 to fully utilize the target instance's CPUs.
  tasks: 64

  # Ensure logs are handled strictly for production-ready debugging.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-specific settings, including the node selector for scheduling.
  pod:
    # This selector targets a specific AWS instance type optimized for HPC workloads.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # When set to false, the job pods are not deleted upon completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection of logs and artifacts.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings required for running on an ARM-based node.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture.
    arch: arm
    # Use an ARM-compatible Flux container image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # A list of containers that will run in each pod of the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # Corrected command:
      # - '-o 3' is changed to the correct '-ok 3' for setting the element order.
      # - '-f' is added to enable the figure of merit (FOM) calculation for performance analysis.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m data/cube_311_hex.mesh -ok 3 -pa -f

      # The working directory is '/app' where the input data files are located.
      workingDir: /app

      # This container provides the workers, not the job launcher.
      # This MUST be false for worker containers.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest fixes the path to the mesh file for the Laghos application.
# The previous attempt failed because the command specified a non-existent 'data/' subdirectory.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as instructed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to 64 to fully utilize the target instance's CPUs.
  tasks: 64

  # Ensure logs are handled strictly for production-ready debugging.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-specific settings, including the node selector for scheduling.
  pod:
    # This selector targets a specific AWS instance type optimized for HPC workloads.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # When set to false, the job pods are not deleted upon completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection of logs and artifacts.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings required for running on an ARM-based node.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture.
    arch: arm
    # Use an ARM-compatible Flux container image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # A list of containers that will run in each pod of the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # Corrected command: The path to the mesh file is updated by removing the 'data/' prefix,
      # as the file resides directly in the working directory.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -ok 3 -pa -f

      # The working directory is '/app' where the input data files are located.
      workingDir: /app

      # This container provides the workers, not the job launcher.
      # This MUST be false for worker containers.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest resolves an application-level error by disabling
# an unsupported performance optimization for the target ARM architecture.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as instructed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to 64 to fully utilize the target instance's CPUs.
  tasks: 64

  # Ensure logs are handled strictly for production-ready debugging.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-specific settings, including the node selector for scheduling.
  pod:
    # This selector targets a specific AWS instance type optimized for HPC workloads.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # When set to false, the job pods are not deleted upon completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection of logs and artifacts.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings required for running on an ARM-based node.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture.
    arch: arm
    # Use an ARM-compatible Flux container image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # A list of containers that will run in each pod of the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # Corrected command: The '-pa' (Partial Assembly) flag is removed. This feature was
      # causing an 'Unknown kernel' error because the required architecture-specific
      # kernels are not available for ARM in this build of the application.
      # Removing the flag forces the application to use a more portable method.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -ok 3 -f

      # The working directory is '/app' where the input data files are located.
      workingDir: /app

      # This container provides the workers, not the job launcher.
      # This MUST be false for worker containers.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest resolves an application-level 'Unknown kernel' error
# by explicitly selecting the 'full assembly' computation method.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as instructed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to 64 to fully utilize the target instance's CPUs.
  tasks: 64

  # Ensure logs are handled strictly for production-ready debugging.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-specific settings, including the node selector for scheduling.
  pod:
    # This selector targets a specific AWS instance type optimized for HPC workloads.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # When set to false, the job pods are not deleted upon completion,
  # allowing for post-run inspection of logs and artifacts.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings required for running on an ARM-based node.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture.
    arch: arm
    # Use an ARM-compatible Flux container image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # A list of containers that will run in each pod of the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos

      # Corrected command: The '-fa' (full assembly) flag is added. This forces the
      # application to use a more general computation method, avoiding the 'Unknown kernel'
      # error caused by the default partial assembly method on the target architecture.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -ok 3 -f -fa

      # The working directory is '/app' where the input data files are located.
      workingDir: /app

      # This container provides the workers, not the job launcher.
      # This MUST be false for worker containers.
      launcher: false
